purpose: Draft the cautious setup script and command sequence for opening the future private PursuitDesk backend repository.
principles: Keep the public tendergrid GitHub Pages repository as the demo and feedback surface.
Create production backend code only in a new private repository.
Write starter files from the v120 file-content export before feature coding starts.
Create labels and milestones before opening generated backend issues.
Run the first workflow once before applying branch protection so required check names are exact.
Never store live secrets in JSON, source control, or setup script output.

commandBlocks.title: Local preflight
commandBlocks.note: Run this before creating anything. It should only read tool versions and GitHub auth state.

commandBlocks.title: Create private repository
commandBlocks.note: Creates the future production backend repo while keeping the public tendergrid demo untouched.
commands: gh repo create dhirajnyse/pursuitdesk-platform --private --description "Private SaaS backend for PursuitDesk"

commandBlocks.title: Create folder skeleton
commandBlocks.note: Creates only the folders needed by the v120 file-content export and setup handoff.

commandBlocks.title: Write starter files
commandBlocks.note: Use the v120 export to create root, API, package, and workflow starter files.
commands: Use data/first-backend-file-content-export.json as the source of truth
Do not write .env or any live secret file
Review generated files before first commit

commandBlocks.title: Create labels and milestones
commandBlocks.note: Backlog metadata should exist before issues are opened.
commands: gh label create area:backend --color 315f93 --description "Backend platform work"
gh label create area:security --color bf3f35 --description "Auth, tenant, access, privacy, audit"
gh label create priority:p0 --color bf3f35 --description "Blocks alpha safety"
gh api repos/dhirajnyse/pursuitdesk-platform/milestones -f title="M0 Repo opens" -f state=open

commandBlocks.title: Install and first proof
commandBlocks.note: The first proof run should show script names and file boundaries before full backend depth exists.

commandBlocks.title: First commit and PR
commandBlocks.note: Commit the skeleton on develop and open the first PR to main with proof output attached.
commands: git commit -m "Initialize PursuitDesk backend alpha shell"
gh pr create --base main --head develop --title "Initialize backend alpha shell" --body-file .github/pull_request_template.md

commandBlocks.title: Apply branch protection after CI names are visible
commandBlocks.note: Required checks should use exact GitHub Actions check names from the first workflow run.
commands: Protect main and require pull request reviews
Require the successful checks mapped in v119
Require staging environment approval before deployment workflows

safetyGates.label: Do not create live production secrets
safetyGates.note: Use test or staging placeholder names until hosting and billing providers are chosen.

safetyGates.label: Do not protect main too early
safetyGates.note: Run the first workflow once, capture exact check names, then apply protection.

safetyGates.label: Do not open issues before labels
safetyGates.note: Create labels and milestones first so imported issues are searchable from day one.

safetyGates.label: Do not mix demo and backend repos
safetyGates.note: The public tendergrid repo remains static; production backend code belongs in pursuitdesk-platform.

safetyGates.label: Do not start feature depth first
safetyGates.note: First commit proves repo shell, tenant, request id, safe errors, audit, redaction, and CI names.

safetyGates.label: Do not paste private keys into JSON
safetyGates.note: The downloadable handoff names secret slots but never contains real values.

safetyGates.label: Do not skip the PR template
safetyGates.note: The first PR should already ask for issue links, proof, release notes, and rollback notes.

safetyGates.label: Do not force branch rules manually blind
safetyGates.note: Branch protection follows the v119 checklist and exact status checks after CI exists.

acceptanceChecks: Script inventory ready: 8 setup script or guide files define the private repo bootstrap pack.
Command order ready: 8 command blocks cover preflight through branch protection.
Folder skeleton ready: 12 folders map directly to v120 starter file paths.
Metadata ready: labels and milestones are available from the repo creation guide.
Issue path ready: generated backend issue bodies can be opened after metadata exists.
Secrets stay manual: secret names are documented without storing values.
Proof path ready: first-run commands define early engineering proof.
Protection timing clear: branch rules wait until workflow check names are visible.
handoff: v121 turns the file-content export into a practical private repo setup script draft.

The setup remains deliberately cautious: create the private repo, create folders, write starter files, create labels and milestones, run proof commands, open the first PR, and only then apply branch protection.
Real secret values stay outside the export. The script only names secret slots so deployment setup remains controlled.
v122 can now generate a richer GitHub labels and milestones import pack so backlog setup becomes even more automatic.
